subject: Animal Husbandry
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory (for candidates in Nigeria); Papers 1 and 2 are a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice questions, all to be answered in 40 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 2: six essay questions drawn from the entire syllabus, each carrying 20 marks; four to be answered in 2 hours for 80 marks. Paper 3: practical paper for school candidates (test of practical work for private candidates), four questions all to be answered in 1 1/2 hours for 60 marks.
excluded: Preamble, aims, requirements, and the lists of facilities, equipment, specimens, charts, drugs and feed samples for practicals.

subtopics.name: Importance of farm animals
objectives: Discuss the source of food (meat, milk, eggs, honey etc.) from farm animals
Discuss raw materials, e.g. hide and skin, bones, hooves, hair/fur, egg shells
Discuss farm animals as a source of manure (fertilizer, bio-gas, bio fuel), growing of maggots and earthworms
Discuss farm animals as a source of feed ingredients: blood meal, bone meal, meat and bone meal, snail shell, egg shell, feathers
Discuss animal power (animal traction, transportation)
Discuss research (laboratory, field), drugs, vaccines, hormones
Discuss employment, sales of products and by-products, and foreign exchange through export of animal products and by-products

Discuss social functions (e.g. bride price, cultural displays), security (ducks, bees, turkeys), pets, sports and games (e.g. horse racing, chicken fighting) and religious festivals (e.g. turkeys, rams)

subtopics.name: Classification of farm animals
objectives: Classify farm animals by stomach type: simple stomach (non-ruminant or monogastric), e.g. poultry, pig, rabbits, horses, donkeys, snails, bees, grasscutters; and complex stomach (polygastric or ruminants), i.e. cattle, sheep and goat

subtopics.name: Identification of ruminants and non-ruminants
objectives: Identify the external features of common ruminants and non-ruminants
Differentiate ruminants from non-ruminants based on type of stomach and type of feed consumed

subtopics.name: Internal organs and their functions in farm animals
objectives: Identify internal organs of farm animals (liver, lungs, heart, kidney, spleen, pancreas, stomach, crop, caecum, gizzard, small intestine, large intestine, tongue, etc.) and state their functions

subtopics.name: Body systems and their functions in farm animals
objectives: Describe the digestive, respiratory, nervous, circulatory, skeletal and reproductive systems
State the functions of each system

subtopics.name: Reproduction in farm animals: definition of terms
objectives: Define terms used in livestock reproduction, including ovulation, oestrus cycle, heat period, signs of heat, mating, gestation, parturition, lactation, colostrum, flushing, steaming up, dystocia, vaginal prolapse

subtopics.name: Reproduction in livestock (mammals)
objectives: Describe detection of heat, mating systems, pregnancy detection and signs of parturition

subtopics.name: Reproduction in poultry
objectives: Describe the process of egg formation in poultry

subtopics.name: Reproductive hormones and their functions
objectives: State the sources and roles of female hormones (oestrogen, progesterone, relaxin, oxytocin, etc.) and male hormones (testosterone/androgen)

subtopics.name: Management of pregnant farm animals
objectives: Describe management of pregnant animals: regular and adequate feeding, body exercise, steaming up, separation from male animals, provision of clean and adequate water, administration of drugs where necessary, dipping to eliminate ecto-parasites, parturition

subtopics.name: Livestock management systems
objectives: Describe the intensive, semi-intensive and extensive systems of livestock management
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each system

subtopics.name: Management practices of livestock
objectives: Describe housing requirements for each of the farm animals and use of local materials for construction of animal houses

Explain management practices: feeding, sanitation, hygiene, castration, dehorning, deworming, vaccination, inoculation, culling, debeaking, smoking (in bees), docking, identification (tattooing, branding, ear-notching, rings, etc.), isolation, weaning and care of the young until weaned
Keep simple records including income and expenditure accounts
Discuss the importance of each practice
Describe management practices from birth to maturity of a named large ruminant, small ruminant, poultry, pigs, grasscutter, bees and snails

subtopics.name: Meaning and classes of animal feeds
objectives: Explain the meaning of animal nutrition
Describe feed nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats and oil, vitamins, minerals and water), their functions, sources and deficiencies in farm animals
Classify animal feeds into concentrates, roughages, supplements, feed additives etc.

subtopics.name: Animal feeds and feeding: livestock rations
objectives: Explain the meaning of livestock rations and their types (balanced, maintenance, production)
Explain malnutrition: meaning, causes and symptoms
State practical ways to check malnutrition: feeding balanced rations, feeding weaker animals separately, deworming, supplementary feeds, feed additives to stimulate appetite
State further control measures: protecting animals from toxic plants and harmful substances, adjusting stocking rates, provision of good quality and adequate water

subtopics.name: Formulation of livestock rations
objectives: Formulate practical diets for different classes of farm animals (starter, grower and finisher diets)
Identify feed ingredients used for diet formulation, e.g. blood meal, fish meal, cotton seed cake, oyster shell, groundnut cake, maize grains, salt, premix, glycine

State factors to consider in feed formulation: physiological status of animal, species, age, body weight, production target, acceptability of feed, nutrient composition, ingredient availability, cost of ingredients

subtopics.name: Processing techniques for different farm animal products
objectives: Describe processing techniques: pre-slaughtering, slaughtering and post-slaughtering activities, and the hygienic conditions required
Explain slaughtering techniques for different farm animals
Process animal products (egg, milk, meat, skin, wool, honey, snail shell, feathers, fur, hooves, horns, blood, faeces/droppings) into other forms (value addition)

subtopics.name: Marketing of animal products
objectives: Describe common marketing channels and agents such as producers, wholesalers, retailers, consumers
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each marketing channel and agent

subtopics.name: Pasture management
objectives: Define pasture and forage crops, give examples and state their importance
Describe the types and features of pasture and forage crops
Explain basic terminologies in pasture management

subtopics.name: Rangeland improvement
objectives: Explain the meaning and features of rangeland
State methods of rangeland improvement: reseeding, rotational grazing, controlled stocking, deferred grazing, controlled burning, fertilizer application, pest control, disease control
State the role of rangeland in livestock production, e.g. provision of vegetation and grasses for animals, exercise, provision of hay and silage

subtopics.name: Meaning and aims of animal improvement
objectives: Explain the meaning and terminologies used in animal improvement
State the aims of farm animal improvement: high reproductive efficiency, potency, mothering ability, cool temperament, high libido, resistance to pests and diseases, tolerance to harsh environment

subtopics.name: Methods of farm animal improvement
objectives: Describe the methods of farm animal improvement: introduction, selection and breeding
State the merits and demerits of each method

subtopics.name: Artificial insemination
objectives: Explain the term artificial insemination
Identify the materials, methods, steps and precautions in carrying out artificial insemination
State the advantages of artificial insemination

subtopics.name: Concept of farm animal disease
objectives: Explain the meaning and causal agents (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa) of diseases in farm animals

subtopics.name: General symptoms of diseases in farm animals
objectives: Describe the signs of a sick animal, e.g. loss of appetite, loss of weight, diarrhoea, high body temperature, blood-stained urine, gnashing of teeth

Recognise further signs: discharges from natural openings, blood-stained faeces, ruffled feathers or fur, standing hair, undue noise, excessive salivation, anaemia, staggering gait, difficulty in breathing, coma, sudden death

subtopics.name: Diseases of farm animals, prevention and control
objectives: Identify the main diseases of farm animals, their causal agents, mode of transmission and symptoms
Describe simple preventive and control measures including the use of antibiotics and ethno-veterinary practices

subtopics.name: Factors predisposing farm animals to diseases
objectives: State factors that predispose farm animals to diseases, e.g. poor nutrition, poor health status, poor sanitation, inadequate bio-security, overcrowding, unfavourable weather conditions, low immunity

subtopics.name: Livestock parasites
objectives: Explain the meaning, classes, control/prevention and effects of parasites on farm animals
Describe the life cycles of parasites
Identify ecto-parasites (ticks, lice, mites, fleas etc.) and endo-parasites (tapeworm, roundworm, hookworm, pinworm, liver fluke, trypanosome etc.) and state their economic importance

subtopics.name: Livestock pests
objectives: Identify livestock pests (rodents, snakes, soldier ants, birds, weevils, termites, flies etc.) and state their effects on farm animals
Describe prevention/control using dewormers, acaricides, pesticides and ethno-veterinary practices
Identify storage pests (rodents, weevils, termites, cockroaches etc.) and field pests (soldier ants, birds, snakes, flies etc.) and state their economic importance

topics.name: Animal Husbandry Practicals
objectives: Carry out and be assessed on the practical skills in the sub-topics below (Paper 3)

subtopics.name: Practical: products and by-products of farm animals
objectives: Identify animal products and by-products such as meat, eggs, milk, honey, hides, skin, blood, hair, wool, feathers, horn, hooves, bones, snail shell, animal dung and state their uses

subtopics.name: Practical: identification of farm animals
objectives: Describe, draw and label the external parts of farm animals

subtopics.name: Practical: internal organs and their functions in farm animals
objectives: Identify and draw the major internal structures in the various body systems of a named ruminant, poultry and pig
State differences in the structures and their functions

subtopics.name: Practical: tools and equipment used in management of farm animals
objectives: Identify tools and equipment used in housing, brooding, feeding, identification, debeaking, castration, handling, dehorning, incubation, milking, slaughtering, and pasture and forage crops
Discuss the maintenance of these tools and equipment

subtopics.name: Practical: feeds and feedstuffs
objectives: Identify common feed ingredients (e.g. maize, groundnut cake, soya bean meal, palm kernel cake, fish meal, bone meal, oyster shell, limestone, salt, salt lick, premix, wheat offal) and the major nutrients they contain
Identify crop residues, agricultural by-products and non-conventional feeds (e.g. jack bean, rumen digesta, cassava peel)

subtopics.name: Practical: pasture and forage crops
objectives: Identify common pasture and forage crops and state their uses
Discuss hay and silage making

subtopics.name: Practical: artificial insemination
objectives: Identify the tools and equipment and their uses
Discuss simple techniques of semen collection, preservation and insemination

subtopics.name: Practical: pests of farm animals
objectives: Identify storage pests and field pests and state their economic importance

subtopics.name: Practical: parasites of farm animals
objectives: Identify ectoparasites and endoparasites and state their economic importance
State the life cycles, prevention and control of these parasites
